facts.statement: Eucnemesaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur named for its robust tibiae.
facts.quote: Eucnemesaurus (; meaning "good tibia lizard", for its robust tibiae) is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur

facts.statement: Eucnemesaurus presumably had the typical prosauropod build of long neck and tail but walked on two legs.
facts.quote: Presumiblemente Eucnemesaurus tuvo la construcción típica de un Prosauropoda, un cuello y una cola largos pero caminando sobre dos piernas

facts.statement: The genus was named in 1920 by Egbert Cornelis Nicolaas van Hoepen based on holotype TM 119.
facts.quote: Eucnemesaurus was named in 1920 by Egbert Cornelis Nicolaas van Hoepen, based on holotype TM 119

facts.statement: Remains were found by Van Hoepen in the Lower Elliot Formation on a farm in Slabberts, South Africa, dating to the Late Triassic (220 to 205 million years ago).
facts.quote: The remains were found by Van Hoepen in a deposit of the Lower Elliot Formation, dated to the Late Triassic (Norian to Rhaetian stages, 220 to 205 million years ago), on a farm in Slabberts, South Africa

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the Greek words eu (well-formed), knemè (tibia), and saurus (lizard).
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego clásico eu, "bien formado", y knemè, "tibia" con saurus, "lagarto"

facts.statement: They lived during the late Triassic, approximately 225 to 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 225 y 210 millones de años, en el Carniense, en lo que hoy es África

facts.statement: The genus is classified within the family Riojasauridae.
Riojasauridae were more closely related to sauropods than to Plateosauridae but more basal than Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Los Riojasauridae estaban más estrechamente relacionados con los saurópodos que con los Plateosauridae, pero más basales que los Massospondylidae

facts.statement: The maxilla once assigned to Aliwalia is not distinct from material belonging to Eucnemesaurus and is clearly from a carnivore.
facts.quote: el maxilar asignado a Aliwalia, no es distinto de otro material, perteneciente a Eucnemesaurus, como lo es claramente de un carnívoro

facts.statement: For many years, the size of the femur led paleontologists to believe Aliwalia was a notably large carnivorous dinosaur for its time.
facts.quote: El tamaño del fémur llevó durante muchos años a muchos paleontólogos a creer que junto con el maxilar claramente carnívoro, ese Aliwalia era el de un dinosaurio carnívoro del tamaño notable para el tiempo en la cual vivió

facts.statement: Specimens of Eucnemesaurus vertebrae have been used in recent studies on the development of skeletal pneumaticity in early dinosaur genera.
facts.quote: Eucnemesaurus vertebral specimens have also been used in recent studies on how skeletal pneumaticity, a trait widespread among saurischian dinosaurs, developed in the earliest dinosaur genera

facts.statement: E. entaxonis differs from E. fortis in adaptations of the femur shaft and lower shin band for rear leg support function.
facts.quote: Esta especie difiere de E. fortis en las adaptaciones en el eje del fémur y en la parte inferior de la banda de la espinilla a una función de apoyo de la pata trasera

rejected.statement: Fossil remains indicate a body length of about 10 to 11 meters and an estimated weight of 1.5 to 2 tons.
rejected.quote: los restos indican una longitud corporal de unos 10 a 11 metros y el peso se estima en 1,50 a 2 toneladas

rejected.statement: Recent studies by Adam Yates justified Eucnemesaurus as a valid genus and a senior synonym to Aliwalia.
rejected.quote: Yates justified Eucnemesaurus as a valid genus and a senior synonym to Aliwalia
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'as a valid genus and a senior synonym'
